relevance_note: Case report of two sisters (Patient 1 and Patient 2) with individual clinical and laboratory detail: 'Additional analysis of plasma and urine creatine and guanidinoacetate using ID LC-MSMS was consistent with GAMT deficiency in both siblings'.
method_note: Read by hand; JSON built with a short script that copies the lab-table rows from the file (checked against the table). Lab table has patients as columns (header '| Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Normal'); full rows quoted so the paper's normal range is in the span. Diagnosis is biochemical only; the paper reports no GAMT genetic testing and prints no variant, so the variants table is empty (no variant is tied to either sister). The paper's text starts mid-sentence at a page break ('sitting tolerance and ease of care... she had not yet received any other medical treatments for her dystonia'); this fragment continues the Patient 2 DBS paragraph ('translating into improved') and is used for Patient 2's treatment summary. Ages: intro gives 'Two female siblings (age 25 and 31 years)' without saying which is which; last-evaluation ages taken from the per-patient sentences ('When seen at age 25 years' for Patient 1, 'When seen at age 30 years' for Patient 2), so 30 vs 31 for Patient 2 may reflect different time points. 'Normal or negative previous investigations included: ... magnetic resonance imaging brain ...' names no patient, so no MRI checklist item is excluded; it also lists amino acids as normal while 'Patient 2 had generalized elevation of urine amino acids' (possible contradiction; only the named finding recorded). Patient 1's 'suspected focal dystonia' is hedged, so dystonia is not reported for her. Patient 1's speech checklist item marked observed from 'occasional words and short phrases' although the authors say she 'has better language skills than is typical'. Developmental delay for Patient 1 based on late speech onset only; intellectual disability not stated for either. Urine GAA for Patient 2 is '...' (not reported). Parents described only as 'related' (consanguinity), not tested or affected, so no rows.
